Follow your Peugeot, Citroën, DS, Opel and Vauxhall cars in Gladys: battery, range, charging,
fuel, mileage, locks. The integration signs in to your MyPeugeot, MyCitroën, MyDS, MyOpel or
MyVauxhall account, like the app, and reads the state your cars last sent to the Stellantis
cloud.

This integration is not affiliated with Stellantis or its brands. It was developed without a car
or an account, from the work of the Home Assistant community: feedback welcome, on the forum or in
the GitHub issues.

## What it does

- One Gladys device per car of the account: electric, plug-in hybrid or combustion.
- Its values are read from the Stellantis cloud every 15 minutes (you can choose 10 to 60). A read
  **never wakes the car**: it returns what the car last sent (when it was switched off, while it
  charges, now and then while parked).
- Nothing is controlled from Gladys yet: preconditioning, charging and locks are shown, not
  commanded (see [Limits](#limits)).
- The GPS position is off by default; you turn it on in the configuration.

## Requirements

- A car of the Stellantis group (Peugeot, Citroën, DS, Opel, Vauxhall) with connected services,
  already added to the brand's app (MyPeugeot, MyCitroën, MyDS, MyOpel, MyVauxhall) and showing its
  state there.
- The e-mail address and password of that app's account.
- **No paid subscription**: the integration only reads the car's state, which the free app and
  the basic connected services allow (a new electric car includes the Connect One pack for several
  years). The paid offers (e-Remote Control, Remote Control, Connect Plus) are only needed for remote
  commands, which this version does not send.
- A **computer** with Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari for the sign-in (once, then again only if the
  session ends): the code is read in the browser's developer tools.
- Gladys 5.1 or later, with access to the Internet.

Fiat, Jeep, Alfa Romeo and the other brands of the group use other apps and another cloud: they are
not covered.

## Configuration

Open **Integrations**, find **Peugeot / Citroën / DS / Opel** and open its **Configuration** tab.

### 1. App and country

| Setting                | What to choose                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| App of the car         | The app you use: MyPeugeot, MyCitroën, MyDS, MyOpel or MyVauxhall.              |
| Country of the account | The country chosen in the app. Vauxhall exists in the United Kingdom only.      |
| Device names language  | Language of the feature names of new devices (French by default).               |
| Refresh                | How often the cloud is read: 10, 15 (default), 30 or 60 minutes.                |
| GPS position           | Off by default. On: the last position the car sent is shown, with a map button. |

**Save** before signing in: the sign-in page depends on the app and the country.

### Sign in

The brands' sign-in page is made for their mobile app: at the end, it hands a code to the app
through an address only the app opens (`mymap://…` for MyPeugeot, `mymacsdk://…` for MyCitroën,
`mymdssdk://…` for MyDS, `mymopsdk://…` for MyOpel, `mymvxsdk://…` for MyVauxhall). On a computer
the browser cannot open it and seems to do nothing, but the address, with the code, appears in its
developer tools. You copy it into Gladys.

1. Click **Connect** (field “Account of the app”): the brand's sign-in page opens in a new tab.
2. In that tab, open the developer tools **before signing in**: `F12`, or `Ctrl+Shift+I`
   (`Cmd+Option+I` on a Mac). Choose the **Console** tab.
3. Sign in with the e-mail address and password of the app, and accept if the page asks for it.
4. The page seems to do nothing: that is expected. Copy the line of the console that contains
   `code=` (see below, browser by browser).
5. Within two minutes (the code expires quickly and works only once), paste it in the action
   **Finish the sign-in** at the bottom of the configuration page, and click it.
6. The action answers “Connected: N vehicle(s)”. Open the **Discovery** tab and add your cars.

Gladys never sees your password: it is typed on the brand's page. The code is traded for a session
that renews itself; it is kept in the integration's storage.

### Chrome and Edge

In the **Console** tab, a red line appears after the sign-in:
`Failed to launch 'mymap://oauth2redirect/fr?code=…&scope=…' because the scheme does not have a registered handler.`
Copy the whole line, or only the address between the quotes.

![Chrome or Edge console: the red line that contains the code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guim31/gladys-stellantis/main/docs/images/console-chrome.svg)

No line? Open the **Network** tab, tick **Preserve log**, sign in again from step 1, then click the
last request (status 302, or the red one named `oauth2redirect…`) and copy the address of its
`location` header, or its URL.

![Network tab: the last request and its location header](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guim31/gladys-stellantis/main/docs/images/network-tab.svg)

### Firefox

In the **Console**, Firefox writes:
`Prevented navigation to “mymap://oauth2redirect/fr?code=…” due to an unknown protocol.`
Copy the address between the quotation marks, or the whole line. If the console is emptied when the
page changes, turn on **Persist Logs** in its settings (gear icon) and sign in again.

![Firefox console: the line that contains the code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guim31/gladys-stellantis/main/docs/images/console-firefox.svg)

### Safari

Turn on the developer tools first: **Safari → Settings → Advanced → Show features for web
developers**. Then, in the sign-in tab, **Develop → Show Web Inspector**, **Network** tab, and tick
**Preserve Log**. After the sign-in, click the last request and copy the `mymap://…` address of its
`Location` header. Safari sometimes also shows the address in an error message of the page.

### What to paste

Any of these works: the whole console line, the address `mymap://oauth2redirect/fr?code=…`, or the
code alone (what follows `code=`, up to `&`). The integration takes the code out of it.

If the action answers “Code refused”: the code was used already, expired, or comes from another
app or country than the ones saved. Click **Connect** again and paste the new code quickly.

The other actions: **Test the connection** lists the cars of the account (no car is woken); **Sign
out** deletes the stored session (the devices stay in Gladys, without new values).

## Devices

Each car is a device named after its model and the end of its VIN, e.g. `Peugeot e-208 (…0208)`:
the full VIN never appears in Gladys or in the logs. A car gets the features its motorization and
its answers allow:

| Feature                 | Cars                       | Value                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Battery level           | electric, plug-in hybrid   | %                                                                                                                                       |
| Electric range          | electric, plug-in hybrid   | km                                                                                                                                      |
| Charging state          | electric, plug-in hybrid   | charging, vehicle connected (charge complete), suspended by the vehicle (waiting), suspended by the charger (failure), idle (unplugged) |
| Plugged in              | electric, plug-in hybrid   | yes / no                                                                                                                                |
| Charging                | electric, plug-in hybrid   | yes / no                                                                                                                                |
| Charging speed          | when the car sends it      | km of range gained per hour (what the app shows; the cloud gives no power in kW)                                                        |
| Charging time remaining | when the car sends it      | minutes (0 when not charging)                                                                                                           |
| Fuel level              | combustion, plug-in hybrid | %                                                                                                                                       |
| Fuel range              | combustion, plug-in hybrid | km                                                                                                                                      |
| Total range             | plug-in hybrid             | km, electric plus fuel                                                                                                                  |
| Mileage                 | when the car sends it      | km                                                                                                                                      |
| Locked                  | when the car sends it      | locked / unlocked (one door unlocked counts as unlocked)                                                                                |
| Door or boot open       | when the car sends it      | yes / no                                                                                                                                |
| Preconditioning         | when the car sends it      | on / off                                                                                                                                |
| Outside temperature     | when the car sends it      | °C                                                                                                                                      |
| GPS position            | when turned on             | `latitude, longitude` text                                                                                                              |

Every feature is read-only. A value that does not change is sent again twice a day, so Gladys keeps
showing it as recent. A value the car stops sending keeps its last state.

## Widget

**My car (Stellantis)** shows one car: battery (or fuel) and range tiles, then a list with the
charge (with its speed and the expected end time while charging), the doors, the preconditioning
and the time of the last update. Its **Refresh** button reads the cloud again (it does not wake the
car); a **Map** button appears when the GPS position is on. Choose the car in the widget's settings.

## Scene trigger

**Charge finished** fires when a car reports a complete charge after a charge in progress. A charge
stopped, failed or ended by unplugging does not fire it. Its variables: the battery level (%) and
the electric range (km). Leave the vehicle filter empty for every car.

Plugged in, unplugged, low battery: use the device's own values in a scene (“device value”
trigger, e.g. _Battery level_ below 20 with “only when the threshold is crossed”), no dedicated
trigger is needed.

## Scene action

**Read a Stellantis car now** reads the state the car last sent to the cloud, at once, and gives the
next actions its battery level, fuel level, total range, plugged in, charging and locked values. It
does not wake the car.

## Scene examples

- **Charge reminder**: every evening at 21:00, _Read a Stellantis car now_, then if the battery
  level is below 30 % and the car is not plugged in, send “Plug the car in” to the family.
- **Charge complete**: trigger _Charge finished_, send “The car is charged:
  \{\{triggerEvent.data.battery_level\}\} %, \{\{triggerEvent.data.range_km\}\} km”.
- **Car left unlocked**: trigger _Locked_ becomes “unlocked”, wait 10 minutes, then if it is still
  unlocked, send a notification.

## Refresh and quotas

The integration reads the cloud on its own timer (one call per car per read, plus a renewal of the
session about once an hour), never through the Gladys poll. Stellantis publishes no quota for this
API; the Home Assistant integration reads every minute without known trouble. If the cloud answers
“too many requests”, reads pause for 30 minutes. A cloud outage is retried after 1, 2, 5, 10 then
every 15 minutes.

## Troubleshooting

- **“Not signed in”**: the sign-in was not finished. Follow [Sign in](#sign-in).
- **“Code refused”**: the code is valid once, about two minutes, for the app and country saved.
  Click **Connect** again, then paste quickly.
- **“No code found”**: paste the line or the address that contains `code=`.
- **“The app of this brand does not exist in this country”**: choose the country of your account
  (Vauxhall: United Kingdom).
- **“The Stellantis session has ended”**: the session was refused when it renewed itself (password
  changed, account reset, long stop of Gladys). Sign in again; the devices and their history stay.
- **No line in the console**: the developer tools were opened after the sign-in. Open them first,
  or use the Network tab with “Preserve log”, and sign in again.
- **A car shows no value, or old values**: the app shows the same: the car sends its state when it
  is switched off, while it charges and now and then; a car unused for days sends less (its 12 V
  battery is protected). A car in **privacy mode** shares nothing: the widget says it.
- **Logs**: the integration writes only its lifecycle at info level. Set `LOG_LEVEL=debug` to see
  every read. Tokens, codes, VINs and positions are never written.

## Limits

- **No remote command yet**: preconditioning, starting or stopping a charge, the charge limit,
  locking, unlocking and waking the car up go through a separate Stellantis service (MQTT) that
  needs an enrolment by SMS code and the PIN of the app. The only open implementations of that
  enrolment are licensed under the GPL; this integration, under Apache 2.0, does not copy them.
  They may come in a later version.
- **Reads only the cloud's state**: no “wake up and refresh”. The values are as recent as the car's
  last message.
- **Sign-in by copying a code**: Stellantis gives no API access to private persons, the integration
  signs in as the brand's app; if Stellantis changes the app's sign-in, the integration may stop
  working until it is updated.
- **Charging speed in km/h**: the cloud gives no power in kW.
- Developed and tested without a car or an account, against answers built from the Home Assistant
  integration: please report what you see.

## How to install Peugeot / Citroën / DS / Opel in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Peugeot / Citroën / DS / Opel appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-stellantis:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-stellantis](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-stellantis).

Peugeot / Citroën / DS / Opel requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Peugeot / Citroën / DS / Opel is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [guim31](https://github.com/guim31), not by the Gladys core team.
